suggestions.rationale: Persistent ringing frequently interferes with falling or staying asleep. Note that sleep impairment is often evaluated as a symptom within a mental health rating rather than as a standalone condition.
evidenceGaps: Treatment records documenting sleep complaints attributed to tinnitus
Whether a separate diagnosis exists or symptoms fall under an existing mental health evaluation
Sleep study if a sleep disorder rather than insomnia is suspected

sourceReferences.note: Schedule of ratings, mental disorders; sleep impairment appears in the general rating formula.

suggestions.rationale: Chronic, unrelenting symptom burden is sometimes linked to anxiety. Requires a diagnosis from a qualified mental health provider.
evidenceGaps: Mental health diagnosis from a qualified provider
Records connecting anxiety onset to tinnitus rather than other stressors
Nexus opinion addressing causation or aggravation

suggestions.rationale: Mood effects are sometimes documented with long-standing, severe tinnitus. If a mental health condition is already service connected, this may affect the existing rating rather than add a new one.
evidenceGaps: Mental health diagnosis from a qualified provider
Documentation of symptom duration and severity
Review of whether an existing mental health rating already covers these symptoms
